Md Khalilur Rahman with Mahbubul Hoque and Afsar Zahan, Advocates ----- For the Petitioner.
Salahuddin Ahmed with Ramjan Ali Sikder, Advocate ----- For the Respondent No.3 
AFM Shahid, Deputy Attorney-General ----- For the Respondent No.2
parties:
Grameen Bank Karmachari Union ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Member, Labour Appellate Tribunal Dhaka and others ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
(a) that respondent No. 2, the Registrar of Trade Union filed an application before the Chairman, Second Labour Court Dhaka under section 10(2) of the Industrial Relations Ordinance, 1969 seeking permission for cancellation of registration of the petitioner's Union on the grounds; (i) that the registration of the Union was obtained by fraud; (ii) by misrepresentation of facts; that the petitioner committed unfair labour practice and that its membership fell below 30%. The said case was registered as IRO case No. 49 of 1991. 

 5. The case was heard in presence of the petitioner as well as respondent Nos. 2 and 3. The petitioner in order to prove its case examined one witness and wanted to examine further witnesses but that was not allowed by the Chairman, Second Labour Court, Dhaka. 

 11. The Member, Labour Appellate Tribunal having heard all the parties dismissed the appeal with findings that the petitioner though did not commit unfair labour practice but the number of its member fell below 30%, and that the Second Labour Court, Dhaka had jurisdiction to accord permission for cancellation of petitioner's registration. 

 12. The petitioner contends that the Second Labour Court, Dhaka had no territorial jurisdiction to entertain the application filed by the Registrar of Trade Union in the present case because both the second parties (i.e. the Grameen Bank Karmachari Union and the Grameen Bank) before the Labour Court had their registered offices at Mirpur within the territorial jurisdiction of the 3rd Labour Court, Dhaka and as per Gazette Notification dated 17th of April, 1986 the 3rd Labour Court, Dhaka had the exclusive jurisdiction to entertain the application and accord permission for cancellation of registration of the petitioner's union; that no notice to show cause was served upon them nor was there any enquiry held in their presence and accordingly, the order passed is against the principle of natural justice; that the finding of the Second Labour Court that the petitioner's membership fell below 30% is wrong in the face of admission of PW 1 to the effect that membership of the petitioner was 5400 before filing of the case and subsequently it rose upto 7562. The petitioner further contended that 22 of the members were compelled to resign from the Union and those resignations came through Mr. Siddique Rahman, Assistant General Manager of respondent No. 3 which constituted unfair labour practice as per provision laid down in section 15 of IRQ and that the Labour Court did not examine any of the members alleged to have resigned in the face of denial by the petitioner; that the case was filed by respondent No. 2 in collusion with respondent No. 3; that there is no proof before the Labour Court that 4487 members of the Union resigned their membership because they never submitted any resignation letter to the President, General Secretary of the Union as required under its constitution. It is further stated that the petitioner Union being the only registered trade union and the only Collective Bargaining Agent briefly CBA, according permission for cancellation of registration of the Union is tantamount to taking away of the right of the employees to form trade union guaranteed under the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh. 

 13. Respondent No. 2 (The Registrar of Trade Unions) has opposed the Rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition giving a general denial of the allegations and assertions made in the writ petition. Respondent No. 3 Grameen Bank has also opposed the Rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition contending, inter alia, that the writ petition is not maintainable inasmuch as a Trade Union cannot maintain an application under Article 102 of the Constitution in its representative capacity as it is not "a person aggrieved" within the meaning of that expression in the Article; that under the Service Rule of the Grameen Bank, the alleged members of the so-called Karmachari Union do not fall within the meaning of "Worker" as defined in the IRO; that the petitioner union was formed with false and fictitious membership of 30% and that they resorted to acts of lawlessness and committed unfair labour practice on 15-5-91 by gheraoing officers and locking the main gate of the Head Office of the Bank, forcibly occupied the premises, prevented the holding of a scheduled international conference of that date; that police had to rush for restoring law and order situation in the premises; that the Second Labour Court had the territorial jurisdiction to hear and dispose of the case inasmuch as the dispute involved the Grameen Bank, having its Head Office at Mirpur with branches all over Bangladesh" and the petitioner union having offices at Mirpur and regional offices elsewhere in different parts of the country, the ease fell within the territorial jurisdiction of Labour Court other than that of the 3rd Labour Court, Dhaka thus conferring jurisdiction upon the Second Labour Court, Dhaka which has exclusive jurisdiction to hear and dispose of cases falling within the limit of more than one Labour court which is exactly the case here. 

 14. Mr. Md Khalilur Rahman, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, has argued that the assumption of jurisdiction by the Second Labour Court was illegal and, as such, the permission that was accorded for cancellation of registration of the petitioner's union was also illegal. He further submits that the petitioner and the second party No. 2 i.e. the Grameen Bank having their registered offices at Mirpur within the territorial jurisdiction of the 3rd Labour Court, Dhaka and the alleged acts of gheraoing offices of the Grameen Bank, locking up of its office and other acts of lawlessness if any, were committed within the local limit of the 3rd Labour Court. In addition to that; resignation letters submitted by a vast majority of the members of the union as alleged by the 1st party was also submitted to the petitioner's office at Mirpur (though denied by the petitioners.) All these facts taken together the instant case clearly fell within the exclusive jurisdiction of the 3rd Labour Court, Dhaka and there is no scope for assuming that this was a case which fell within the concurrent jurisdiction of the 3rd Labour Court as well as labour courts within or beyond Dhaka where the union has its Zonal offices and members scattered all over Bangladesh. Mr. Rahman confined his argument only to the point of lack of jurisdiction of the Second Labour Court. 

 "1. 1st Labour Court, Dhaka (a) Tejgaon, Gulshan, Ramna and Motijheel Police Stations of Dhaka Metropolitan Area and Keranigonj, Savar, Dohar, Nawabganj, and Dhamrai Upazilas of Dhaka District. 

 2. Second Labour Court, Dhaka (a) Demra, Sutrapur Kotwali Police Station of Dhaka Metropolitan Area. 

 3. 3rd Labour Court, Dhaka (a) Lalbagh, Mirpur, Mohammadpur and Dhanmondi Police Stations of Dhaka Metropolitan Area and other areas of Dhaka Metropolitan Area which are not included within the jurisdiction of 1st and 2nd Labour Court. 

 17. From the above re-specification of jurisdiction it is thus clear that the instant case fell within the exclusive jurisdiction of the 3rd Labour Court, Dhaka. Therefore when a court exercises jurisdiction which is beyond its territorial limits that exercise of jurisdiction is void and the order passed is tainted with coram non-judice. In the instant case the according of permission for cancellation of registration of the petitioners' union by the Second Labour Court is clearly without jurisdiction. It is well settled that the situation of the registered office of a company or for that matter a Registered Trade Union fixes domicile of the company and one of the tests which has been laid down, so far a trading company is concerned, is whether the directing power resides on, in the expressive language of Foot, where the brain which controls the operation of the Company is situated "(Cheshire Private International Law, 1938 Edition at page 198). Admittedly the petitioners union is a registered trade union and a body corporate and, as such, it is a juristic person and hence it can sue and be sued in its own name. 

 19. We are required to see where the cause of action arose. As regards the allegations of gheraoing the office of Grameen Bank, admittedly it took place at Mirpur within the territorial jurisdiction of the 3rd Laobur Court. As regards the second allegation that membership of the petitioner union in consequence of mass resignation fell below 30%, both the labour Court and the Labour Appellate Tribunal held that true copies of resignation letters were submitted to the labour Court by the Registrar thus suggesting that the original resignation letters were submitted to the office of the union (which, of course, was denied by the petitioner). By ignoring the denial of the petitioner as to submission Of resignation letters to their office at Mirpur if it is accepted the resignation letters, in fact, were submitted to the registered office of the union thus bringing down the membership strength of the union below the required 30%, even then the facts remain that those resignation letters were submitted to a place which is situated within the territorial jurisdiction of the 3rd Labour Court, Dhaka (where the registered office of the union is situated). So, on both counts it appears that the cause of action arose at Mirpur which is within the exclusive territorial jurisdiction of the 3rd Labour Court, Dhaka. 

 20. If we, are to accept the argument of the learned Advocate for the respondents that although the act of gheraoing of the Head Office of Grameen Bank took place at Mirpur within the local limits of the 3rd Labour Court, the resignation letters were sent from different parts of the country by members residing all over Bangladesh and that the union also carries on its business from various zonal offices outside Dhaka and as such Labour Courts other than the 3rd Labour Court, Dhaka have also jurisdiction to entertain the complaint filed by the Registrar of Trade Unions for according permission to cancel registration of the Union. This interpretation, we are constrained to say, cannot be accepted without a great amount of violence upon the statute itself. The main thrust of the argument of the learned Advocate for the respondents and the reasoning of both the courts below were on the consideration that the concerned trade union carries on business not only from its registered office at Dhaka but also from its zonal offices beyond Dhaka, thus jurisdiction is not confined to the 3rd Labour Court Dhaka alone. The answer to this is found in the words of "Foot" quoted above i.e. the registered office being the brain controlling the operation of the company or the trade union fixes the domicile which term is relevant for jurisdiction over it. 

 21. In the instant case had the allegation of gheraoing the office taken place somewhere other than Dhaka, say for example at Tangail where, according to the respondents, the petitioner has its zonal office, obviously the labour court of that area would have territorial jurisdiction and in that event law would have conferred jurisdiction upon the Second Labour Court, Dhaka on the simple logic that even though the petitioner union situated within the territorial jurisdiction of the 3rd Labour Court, Dhaka, the case having fallen within the jurisdiction of more than one Labour court i.e. 3rd Labour Court Dhaka and the 1st Labour Court Dhaka, the case would attract the jurisdiction of the 2nd Labour Court, Dhaka which is not the situation here in the present case. 

 22. To enable the 2nd Labour Court, Dhaka to assume jurisdiction in this case, it was imperative upon the respondents to show that the events and occurrences giving rise to the cause of action took place within the jurisdiction of more than one labour court. From the facts and circumstances of the present case we find that the alleged incident took place within the exclusive jurisdiction of the 3rd Labour Court, Dhaka i.e. within Mirpur.
